math_plain: Score the expected profit a validator coalition gains from hiding blocks versus adopting the standard honest strategy.
why_math: Miners only care about which choice earns more; by calculating exact expected payoffs, you can find which strategy dominates. If profit exceeds the honest payout, that strategy is adopted.

following the slope downhill to improve
math_plain: Craft malicious documents that are semantically similar to user queries yet maximize token consumption during inference.
why_math: The attack works by poisoning retrieval so the model fetches long, complex documents; optimizing document tokens directly targets the resource bottleneck. Learning agents can discover which phrases trigger maximum token explosion.

math_tags: matching and allocating who gets what
math_plain: Select vertices with limited lifespans to cover edges, where a vertex at time t covers edges until time t plus duration minus one.
why_math: This is a temporal matching problem: you match protective coverage to dangerous edges, but coverage expires. The lifespan constraint turns static vertex cover into a scheduling problem solvable via layer-by-layer approximation.

math_tags: finding the settings with least error
smart random sampling and averaging
math_plain: Solve the fractional allocation online, then round to integers using controlled randomness to preserve the cost guarantee.
why_math: Rounding works because fractional solutions are easier to compute and remain feasible; randomized rounding spreads the fractional excess to integers while keeping expected cost unchanged.

math_plain: Train language models on historical character biographies to generate authentic role-playing dialogue.
why_math: Character behavior patterns exist in historical texts; learning these patterns allows models to predict plausible responses consistent with documented lives.

math_plain: Test whether AI repair systems can match ground-truth output by iteratively applying fixes until code execution succeeds.
why_math: Repairs work by exploiting the structure of common failures: missing dependencies, path issues, logic gaps. A system that learns these patterns can address each type. Success requires output equivalence, not just execution.

math_plain: Score how well the model's extracted graph structure matches the correct relationship directions between entities.
why_math: Hallucinations show up as wrong edge directions; by treating the correct graph and extracted graph as two configurations and measuring their alignment distance, you separate correct from corrupted structures.

math_plain: Model opinion propagation as a point process where opinions flow at rates determined by emotional context and hierarchical position.
why_math: Opinion spreads in bursts when emotions align, modeled as time-clustered events; the rates reveal how hierarchy and feeling drive adoption. This captures that propagation speed depends on both content and audience readiness.

math_tags: learning a function from examples
math_plain: Standardize preprocessing and evaluation across multiple foundation models on structured tabular data.
why_math: Different models use different formats; unifying them reveals which algorithm genuinely works best on a given task by removing implementation noise.

learning by comparison of similar and different
math_plain: Map images and text to a shared space where groups of semantically similar samples sit close together, then retrieve across modalities.
why_math: Hypergraphs capture that many images share one concept with many texts; placing such groups close makes retrieval exact—finding one similar sample finds the whole related group.

math_plain: Learn which tools best match user intent by optimizing a reward signal from successful tool calls on diverse queries.
why_math: Tool selection is a ranking problem; trial-and-error with reward feedback discovers which features of a query predict tool match. Reinforcement learning works because success/failure is directly observable.

math_plain: Recommend intermediate articles that balance current interest alignment with gradual drift toward a target topic, weighted by the user's openness.
why_math: Users resist radical shifts but accept gradual ones; weighting by openness prevents rejection. Intermediate articles act as stepping stones, each one slightly closer to the target than the last.

math_plain: Ask targeted clarification questions to eliminate competing interpretations of an ambiguous query.
why_math: Ambiguous queries map to multiple solution subgraphs; each question collapses possibilities by revealing which graph region the user meant. Efficient probing asks only questions that split remaining hypotheses.

math_tags: finding the settings with least error
following the slope downhill to improve
math_plain: Train networks in regions where small input changes cause small output changes, measured by the flatness of the loss landscape.
why_math: Sharp valleys predict poor generalization: a network tuned to a narrow optimum breaks when data shifts slightly. Flat minima are stable—small perturbations barely change the loss, so the network generalizes.

math_tags: measuring surprise and information
math_plain: Identify visual design choices—color, layout, symbolic encoding—that do not directly represent data yet improve insight and engagement.
why_math: Visual properties work because they exploit how humans process information: color evokes emotion, layout guides attention, symbols encode meaning. These channels communicate beyond the numbers alone.
